result.text:
I saved the competitor discovery artifact with **three candidate companies across four product pages**. The pages identify themselves as synthetic fixtures, so the shortlist does **not** verify commercial availability or pricing in Germany or the Netherlands. [EX-0031, EX-0043, EX-0060, EX-0073]

| Candidate | Pricing as stated on the fixture page |
|---|---|
| **Corvane Group — Presence P1** | USD 199 per unit as a launch offer; occupancy insights at USD 7 per sensor per month, billed annually. Corvane’s page identifies Presence P1 as the renamed OccuPoint, so Brightfield Analytics is not counted separately. [EX-0025, EX-0028, EX-0029] |
| **Noctra — Air** | Quote only. The product estimates meeting-room occupancy from motion and CO₂ rise. [EX-0038, EX-0040] |
| **Tallyway — Beam** | USD 189 per counter; dashboard at USD 5 per counter per month, billed annually. It counts entries and exits at the doorway rather than sensing seated occupants directly. [EX-0050, EX-0054, EX-0055] |

Tallyway illustrates why battery claims need their test conditions: its page specifies **7 years at one report every 10 minutes**, but **14 months at one report per minute**, below the two-year benchmark. [EX-0058, EX-0012]

Manual alternatives remain unverified. The saved artifact is a discovery shortlist, not a validated market or customer-feedback comparison.

result.text:
I reread both product pages, but couldn’t save the Corvane Group profile: the artifact store rejected the write because another research instance owns that profile.

| Page and publication date | One-off sensor price | Occupancy insights |
|---|---|---|
| Corvane Presence P1, 2026-09-15 | USD 199 per unit, launch offer [EX-0028] | USD 7 per sensor per month, billed annually [EX-0029] |
| Brightfield OccuPoint, 2026-04-02 | USD 229 per unit [EX-0070] | USD 7 per sensor per month, billed annually [EX-0071] |

The one-off hardware prices differ on the same per-unit basis; the subscription prices agree. Both pages describe battery-powered thermal and PIR sensing and claim **up to 3 years** of battery life [EX-0030, EX-0067, EX-0072]. Cabling requirements, still-occupant accuracy, privacy practices, and installer effort remain unknown from the two pages reviewed.

Both pages identify themselves as synthetic fixtures, not real offers [EX-0031, EX-0073].

tests.method: Compare sensor output against observer ground truth during seated reading and calls across mounting positions.

threshold.value: Zero false vacancy events in 20 half-hour occupied trials.

cite.quote: Battery life of two years or more is the line buyers ask about first.

tests.label: inference
tests.method: Log current draw under representative busy-office reporting, retries and temperature; estimate service life using usable battery capacity and audit power requirements.

threshold.value: At least 24 months projected service life and no new power or network cabling at the sensor.

cite.quote: No image may leave the device.

tests.method: Inspect documented data flows and verify outbound payloads during setup, normal operation and diagnostics; request works-council documentation.

threshold.value: Zero image payloads observed and written documentation covering all outbound data flows.
